title: J15 Candidates
methodology: October 19 independent dynasty ranking of all 19 players currently on this page. The 17 reported 2027 J15 candidates are compared with Shoki Oda (conditional U.S. route; class not established) and Tatsuya Nogami (confirmed October 2026 signing). Board rank is not a pure 2027 class rank or an external publication ranking. Compare offensive upside, credible contact/decisions, game impact, athletic contributions, defensive opportunity and development risk; treat bonuses as context rather than a score. Pitching receives an attrition and role-translation discount. Sparse coverage is disclosed through confidence and must not automatically be read as weak talent. Adjacent rankings within tiers are especially uncertain. Existing supplied scouting, newly accessible reporting and Pipeline interpretation are distinguished in each research check. BA direct article access was blocked; indexed excerpts and attributed secondary coverage were reviewed, and no complete proprietary article or ranking is reconstructed. No new professional measurements, tool grades, outcome probabilities, calculator values or draft eligibility are assigned.

players.name: Alfredo Sena
scoutingParagraphs: Sena leads this working class on the strength of a broad offensive and defensive package. The supplied scouting research describes an advanced approach, strong control of the barrel and substantial bat speed, alongside speed and an arm that support a shortstop future.

An impact everyday shortstop is the favorable outcome. That projection still rests on amateur looks: adjustment to professional pitching, physical development and the conversion of tools into game production remain unresolved. His expected Atlanta destination is not an official signing.

Pipeline interpretation: the attractive combination is offensive flexibility with a premium defensive route. If his reported barrel control holds against breaking balls and changing speeds, he could produce value through contact and on-base ability before mature power arrives. If the swing needs a larger adjustment, the athletic foundation would still give him development options, but it would not establish a safe offensive floor. An impact everyday shortstop is a ceiling scenario, not a player comparison or a guaranteed role.

What would change the evaluation: repeated competitive looks showing how he handles quality spin, whether his impact comes without sacrificing contact, and how his lateral mobility develops as he gains strength. Once he signs and plays professionally, batted-ball distribution and performance against age-appropriate competition will be more useful than bonus headlines. No verified exit velocities, chase rates, stolen-base projection or MLB arrival date are available here.

players.name: Eudi Yuten
scoutingParagraphs: Yuten is a switch-hitting Dominican shortstop linked to Seattle’s 2027 class. Accessible Seattle Sports reporting describes top-five class standing, while attributed international reporting highlights a broad athletic tool package. These labels establish a prominent amateur evaluation, not measured five-tool grades.

The previous low placement over-weighted the scarcity of public tool detail. A high-upside shortstop deserves inclusion with the leading group, while the actual hit/power split and consistency from both sides remain unclear. Expected destination and external reputation are distinct from a completed signing or a verified offensive floor.

Pipeline interpretation: the uncertainty is unusually concentrated in the scouting detail. Being described as a highly regarded switch-hitting shortstop establishes visibility, but it does not tell us which offensive tool carries the profile, how the two swings compare or whether shortstop is likely to remain his position. A middle-infield outcome is a possibility to investigate, rather than an established forecast supported by measured tools.

What would change the evaluation: an attributable, dated report describing contact quality, power, running and defense, followed by competitive looks from both sides of the plate. Those details could justify substantial movement in either direction. The current working rank should not be read as a refutation of outside top-of-class descriptions; a definitive class consensus cannot be calculated from the limited evidence. Bonus size alone will not settle the gap.

players.name: Shoki Oda
scoutingParagraphs: October 15, 2026 update: Oda announced his intention to pursue baseball in the United States. Nikkan Sports reports that an American university remains an option alongside a minor-league route. He has not announced an MLB agreement or college commitment. U.S. intentions do not establish a January 2027 signing.

Identity and background: the 18-year-old Yokohama High School right-hander is from Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, and represented Japan U18 at the September 2026 BFA Asian Championship. Samurai Japan lists 186 cm and 81 kg (approximately 6 feet 1 inch and 179 pounds), batting and throwing right-handed. These are listed measurements, not a new physical assessment.

Fastball development: dated reporting documents a 152 km/h peak in 2025, 154 km/h in spring 2026 and 157 km/h (97.6 mph) in summer 2026. The reported Koshien peak was 156 km/h (96.9 mph). These are maximum readings, not average or sustained starter velocity; further gains are not assumed. The supplied earlier 148 km/h checkpoint lacks a verified date and is not included as an established measurement.

Arsenal: Japanese amateur scouting coverage reports a slider in the 130s km/h, changeup in the 120s, curveball in the upper 110s and a forkball. These are reported amateur pitch labels and approximate ranges, not professional tracking measurements. No pitch grades, usage, spin, movement or Stuff+ figures are assigned.

Spring 2026 sample — supplied secondary compilation: seven outings, 44.0 IP, 43 strikeouts, 10 walks and a reported 2.05 ERA. Derived rates are 8.80 K/9, 2.05 BB/9 and 4.30 K/BB. These figures come from the supplied research brief; the linked compilation’s accessible text does not independently expose that complete spring subtotal. Keep this provisional sample separate from official tournament records and other seasons.

September 2026 U18 sample — Chinese Taipei: six innings, three hits, one run and seven strikeouts; the linked secondary tournament analysis additionally reports five walks. The official game report supports the innings, hits and strikeouts. This was one start against a strong international opponent, not a season-level command estimate.

Pipeline interpretation: premium reported velocity, multiple secondaries and U18 experience support starting-pitcher upside. Sustained velocity, fastball bat-missing ability, a consistent secondary out pitch, command against patient hitters and adaptation to professional workloads remain the key questions. Seven strikeouts and five walks in the Taiwan outing illustrate both upside and remaining strike-throwing risk.

Acquisition route: a direct international amateur agreement could place him in a future J15 pool, potentially 2027; neither that class nor a January 15 signing is confirmed. If he chooses a U.S. university, future MLB Draft eligibility must be checked after enrollment and under the applicable rules. Do not assume the 2027 MLB Draft. He is excluded from the published domestic BA/DD draft consensus and confirmed FYPD pool.

Interest versus agreement: MLB scouting attention is documented, but no club is assigned here. Reported team interest and speculative bonus discussions are not offers, signed agreements or paid bonuses. Organization, signing bonus, official grades and fantasy eligibility remain unconfirmed.

Next checkpoint: monitor the October 22, 2026 NPB Draft and subsequent career announcements, then reliable confirmation of an MLB signing or U.S. college enrollment. A Japanese pro-intent filing alone does not establish a commitment to NPB. ETA remains TBD — unsigned amateur.

players.name: Mairon De La Rosa
scoutingParagraphs: De La Rosa combines switch-hitting ability with an explosive athletic profile. Prior research highlights speed, bat speed and power projection, with enough arm and movement to retain a shortstop path. Evaluators have differed on which side of the plate is more advanced.

The ceiling is a power-and-speed middle infielder, but barrel consistency and pitch recognition will determine how much of that package reaches games. The working placement rewards the breadth of his tools without treating potential as established production. Seattle is an expected signing destination.

Pipeline interpretation: switch-hitting creates two development tracks. Contact quality, decisions and swing consistency need to be assessed separately from each side; a favorable look from one side does not settle the other. The power-and-speed ceiling is attractive because several offensive paths could contribute, but the current record does not establish how often he will reach base or turn athletic speed into stolen bases.

What would change the evaluation: competitive evidence that he can recognize spin, stay on pitches outside his preferred location and produce hard contact from both sides. Defensive repetitions will help determine whether the shortstop projection survives physical growth. A stronger hit foundation would narrow his outcome range; increasing swing-and-miss would make the exciting tools less accessible. Those are development checkpoints, not measured current weaknesses.

players.name: Miguel Grullon
scoutingParagraphs: Grullon's case begins with a promising offensive foundation. The supplied research emphasizes approach and barrel accuracy, with increasing strength giving the bat more power potential. He is currently discussed as a center fielder, although a future move to right field is possible.

An everyday outfielder with a useful blend of contact and power is the upside. A corner assignment would raise the offensive bar, so game power matters alongside contact quality. Neither a home-run total nor an MLB arrival date is established by these amateur reports. Texas remains an expected destination.

Pipeline interpretation: his profile hinges on whether growing strength complements the reported barrel accuracy. Maintaining contact while adding useful airborne impact would create a more complete offensive package than strength alone. Center-field retention would give the bat more margin; a move to right field would place greater weight on extra-base production. Neither outcome should be assumed from an amateur position label.

What would change the evaluation: repeated looks against better velocity and breaking balls, evidence of hard contact beyond pulled mistakes, and updated running and defensive evaluations after physical growth. An early home run is an encouraging observation, not proof of a future power grade. The first professional sample should be judged for contact quality and decisions before using a short run of home runs to redraw his ceiling.

players.name: Jesus Arteaga
scoutingParagraphs: Arteaga offers a different route to value from the athletic shortstops in this class. Prior scouting research describes a selective bat with extra-base impact, paired with an advanced receiving-and-throwing foundation and a strong arm.

The favorable outcome is a catcher whose bat supports regular playing time while his defense keeps him behind the plate. Catcher development is rarely linear, and offensive performance against professional pitching is still untested. Tampa Bay is an expected agreement, not a completed signing.

Pipeline interpretation: a selective bat gives Arteaga an offensive identity distinct from a catcher whose value rests mainly on strength. For dynasty purposes, the relevant question is whether selection turns into productive contact rather than simply passivity. Keeping the receiving and throwing foundation while the bat advances would create a regular-catching path, although no professional workload or durability history is established here.

What would change the evaluation: game evidence of blocking, receiving consistency, release accuracy and the ability to sustain offensive quality while catching frequently. The hitting checkpoints are recognition of spin and enough damage on hittable strikes. If catching remains viable, moderate offensive production can have a different fantasy value than the same bat at first base. That positional inference is conditional; no move away from catcher is asserted.

players.name: Nicolas Quintero
scoutingParagraphs: Quintero's appeal is a combination of contact feel, patience and emerging pull-side power. The research describes fluid infield actions and a useful arm, while continued physical growth could shift his eventual defensive home from shortstop to third base.

The bat could support an everyday infield role if contact and power develop together. A move down the defensive spectrum would increase the amount of offensive impact required. His amateur profile leaves both the positional outcome and the timing of development open. San Diego is the expected destination.

Pipeline interpretation: contact feel and patience are most valuable if they allow Quintero to reach pitches he can drive. Pull-side power is a potential route to impact, but a pull-oriented approach can become easier to attack if opposite-field contact and pitch recognition do not develop. The current notes support questions about how the package fits together, rather than a verified contact rate or a settled offensive grade.

What would change the evaluation: updated game looks documenting decisions, contact against spin and whether added strength improves impact without slowing his infield movement. If he grows into third base, the same bat would need more sustained damage to support an everyday role. Keeping shortstop would improve the defensive pathway, but it would not independently prove an impact dynasty bat. Independent reporting remains thin in this update.

players.name: Junior Fortunato
scoutingParagraphs: Fortunato is a left-handed outfielder whose supplied scouting notes emphasize discipline and developing home-run power. Center field remains part of the projection, with arm strength providing an alternative route to right field as his frame develops.

An everyday outfielder is a plausible upside outcome if strike-zone judgment translates and game power emerges. The current evidence does not establish either an MLB hit tool or a firm defensive destination. Toronto is a reported expected agreement; official organization and professional results remain pending.

Pipeline interpretation: the left-handed power route is the clearest offensive opportunity, while the reported arm offers a possible corner-field fit if center field becomes less likely. The central question is how consistently he can bring that power into games without losing contact or expanding the zone. Public descriptions of multiple tools should be treated as a starting point for evaluation; they do not establish a high-probability everyday outcome.

What would change the evaluation: sustained competitive contact, recognition of breaking pitches and updated defensive speed as his body develops. A corner-field outcome would demand more from the bat than center field. Early professional strikeouts and walks will need sample-size and league context, and arm strength alone cannot establish defensive quality. No verified sprint time, batted-ball metric or numerical Pipeline grade is assigned.

players.name: Dylan Rodriguez
scoutingParagraphs: Rodriguez is a right-handed catcher with a promising offensive foundation in the supplied research. Feel for contact and bat speed support the bat, while the defensive side of the profile is described as less developed at this stage.

A regular catcher with offensive value is the favorable projection if the receiving and throwing progress alongside the bat. A move away from catcher would change the fantasy profile and raise the offensive threshold. Cincinnati is an expected destination; professional evidence is still pending.

Pipeline interpretation: the bat and catching development need to be followed separately. Contact feel and bat speed could support an offensive catcher, but they cannot substitute for receiving progress or establish future playing time. The current notes make the defensive pathway less settled than Arteaga’s; that is a distinction in the supplied research, not a newly assigned defensive grade.

What would change the evaluation: updated receiving, blocking and throwing observations, plus game contact against spin and changing speeds. Keeping catcher eligibility would materially affect the fantasy translation of his bat. If a different position eventually becomes necessary, the offensive standard would change and the projection would need a new evaluation. Unrelated U.S. high-school players with the same name are excluded from this profile.

Pipeline interpretation: Hernandez represents a power-led outcome with a large dependence on usable contact. The supplied notes raise recognition and swing-and-miss questions, but no measured miss rate is available. The present evidence cannot select one or assign a probability of improvement.

What would change the evaluation: game looks against breaking balls and quality velocity, evidence that he can adjust with two strikes, and updated defensive movement as he grows. If second or third base becomes the destination, power will need to be accompanied by enough on-base ability to sustain playing time. Raw impact can support a favorable ceiling while still leaving a wide range of outcomes. No statistics from older players sharing his name are used.

players.name: Euniel De La Cruz
scoutingParagraphs: De La Cruz brings an aggressive offensive approach, bat speed and pull-side impact to the supplied research. The swing has substantial moving parts, making repeatability an important question. Shortstop and third base both remain possible defensive outcomes.

An impact infield bat is the ceiling if swing consistency and decisions improve together. The present uncertainty is how frequently he will access that impact against better pitching; raw bat speed alone does not answer it. The Mets are the expected signing destination, not an official organization assignment.

Pipeline interpretation: the combination of bat speed, aggression and pull-side impact creates a high-impact possibility, with timing and selectivity central to whether it becomes playable. Moving parts do not automatically mean a poor swing; the question is whether he can repeat the movement against changing speeds. Likewise, aggression is useful when it produces damage on strikes and costly when it expands the zone. No measured chase or contact rate settles either question.

What would change the evaluation: repeated competitive looks showing swing adjustability, strike-zone decisions and contact when pitchers avoid his preferred pull-side locations. Updated body and defensive evaluations will help distinguish shortstop from third base. A corner-infield outcome would raise the offensive requirement, making consistent game power especially important. The ceiling remains an impact infield bat, but assigning a home-run total or a specific MLB comparison would overstate this evidence.

players.name: Tatsuya Nogami
scoutingParagraphs: Signed Padres developmental sleeper: a 20-year-old Japanese right-hander with reported upper-90s peak velocity and a splitter, arriving from Osaka Sangyo University’s semi-hardball program. The arm strength warrants deep-league attention, but professional command, pitch quality and starter durability remain unproven. High-upside lottery ticket; very high risk and no firm MLB ETA.

MLB confirms the October 15 minor-league deal. Nikkan Sports identifies a January 6, 2006 birth date and an unusual route through Japanese university semi-hardball. Its 156 km/h peak converts to about 97 mph. The university federation previously documented 155 km/h in a May game and named a splitter, slider, cutter and two-seamer. These support legitimate arm-strength interest, but neither source supplies a professional average fastball, movement profile or measured pitch grades. MLB lists 6-foot-3 and 190 pounds; Japanese reports vary slightly in size.

Semi-hardball uses a different ball, and success in that environment cannot be translated directly into affiliated-baseball strikeouts or run prevention. The reported spring strikeout sample is encouraging but lacks a walk total and professional opposition. A multi-pitch amateur repertoire also does not prove that each offering will survive against better hitters. The first priorities are fastball velocity over full outings with the professional ball, splitter separation and strike throwing. Rotation development is possible; relief, organizational depth and failure to reach MLB remain material paths.

For deep dynasty formats, this is an upside stash rather than a near-term fantasy starter. A credible starting path would require repeatable command, a usable breaking pitch and workload growth; a fastball/splitter combination could instead support relief if it misses professional bats. That bullpen possibility matters in BangaLangin, where replaceable relievers have limited trade value. Risk is very high and confidence in a specific future role is low. Revisit after an affiliate assignment, verified pro velocity and pitch data, innings, walks, strikeouts and health reports. His comparison rank here is separate from the NPB/KBO candidate board.
